findings.basis: Rule round 62, item 1, group 2. M1 525-03, 1 bundle. The Google word is one barbet baseline dated 2024-06-30. m1_sg is silent on the 33 other models read, on every date from 2022-09 to 2026-10-15, and in the served lane, and none of the 16 trees naming the code sets false.
findings.effect: Android's default is true (CarrierConfigManager.java:2515,12089). shouldHoldForEmergencyCall (TelephonyConnectionService.java:3704-3714) reads the config of the phone placing the emergency call. With false it hangs up the other calls first (:2392-2408), on a dual SIM phone those on the other SIM too. With true it holds them and dials. Telecom reads the key per ongoing call's account (CallSequencingController.java:1016-1037) and fills a missing key with true (CallsManager.java:4623-4647). With false Telecom waits up to 5 s per call for the disconnect, and a timeout or a failed disconnect aborts the emergency call (VerifyCallStateChangeTransaction.java:44, CallsManager.java:2458), and nothing redials it. With true a hold nobody answers makes the call wait. Neither value is shown safer for the emergency call; the only certain cost of false falls on the other call, which is lost. Read, not tested.
findings.risk: No harm was found. A hold changes the other call's fate: the phone holds it instead of dropping it, as a Pixel does on these SIMs. Nothing here says what the network does.
